title: Netaji Bhawan | Kolkata Trips
description: Discover Netaji Bhawan in Kolkata, the ancestral home of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose. Learn about its history, museum, timings, entry fee.
textContent: Netaji Bhawan Netaji Bhawan is one of Kolkata’s most significant historical landmarks and a must-visit destination for anyone interested in India’s freedom movement. Located on Lala Lajpat Rai Sarani (formerly Elgin Road), this iconic house was the ancestral residence of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, one of India’s greatest freedom fighters. Today, it serves as a museum and research centre, preserving priceless artifacts, photographs, documents, and memories associated with his extraordinary life. The highlight of the museum is the legendary Wanderer car used by Netaji during his daring escape from British surveillance on the night of 16 January 1941, an event that altered the course of India’s independence movement. Whether you are a history enthusiast, student, or traveler exploring Kolkata, Netaji Bhawan offers an inspiring glimpse into the life and legacy of one of India’s most respected national heroes. Why Visit Netaji Bhawan? Ancestral home of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose. Witness the famous Wanderer car used during his historic escape. Explore galleries showcasing rare photographs and personal belongings. Learn about the Indian National Army (INA) and Azad Hind Movement. Visit one of Kolkata’s most important heritage museums. Excellent destination for students, researchers, and history lovers. History of Netaji Bhawan The Bose family built the house in 1909, and it remained the family residence for decades. Netaji spent many important years of his life here before becoming one of India’s leading freedom fighters. During the British Raj, Netaji was frequently placed under house arrest because of his revolutionary activities. On 16 January 1941, while confined by British authorities, he secretly escaped from this very house disguised as a Pathan. Assisted by his nephew Sisir Kumar Bose, Netaji travelled in the family’s German-made Wanderer car to Gomoh Railway Station (now Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Gomoh), from where he began his remarkable journey that eventually led him to Germany and later Southeast Asia to organize the Indian National Army. Following India’s independence, the residence was transformed into a memorial and museum dedicated to preserving Netaji’s remarkable legacy. Architecture and Design Netaji Bhawan is a beautiful early 20th-century Bengali mansion featuring colonial architectural influences. Some notable architectural elements include: Elegant colonial façade Spacious verandahs Traditional wooden staircases Period furniture Large family rooms converted into museum galleries Historical photographs displayed throughout the building The museum has been carefully preserved to retain much of its original character while incorporating modern exhibition spaces. Museum Highlights One of the major attractions of Netaji Bhawan is the Netaji Research Bureau Museum, established by Dr. Sisir Kumar Bose in 1957. Visitors can explore: Wanderer Car The most iconic exhibit is the original German-made Wanderer car that Netaji used during his dramatic escape in January 1941. Personal Belongings The museum displays: Clothing Personal furniture Spectacles Letters Diaries Books Medals Household items Rare Photographs Numerous photographs document: Netaji’s childhood Family life Political career Congress presidency International travels Formation of the Indian National Army INA Gallery Dedicated exhibits showcase: Azad Hind Government INA uniforms Military insignia Maps Documents Campaign history Library and Archives Researchers can access a rich collection of books, manuscripts, newspapers, and historical documents related to Netaji and India’s freedom movement. Netaji’s Great Escape Perhaps the most fascinating chapter associated with Netaji Bhawan is Netaji’s legendary escape. On the night of 16 January 1941, while under strict British surveillance, Netaji disguised himself as Mohammad Ziauddin, a Pathan insurance agent. Accompanied by his nephew Sisir Kumar Bose, he quietly left the house in the Wanderer car and travelled nearly 500 km to Gomoh railway station. This daring operation enabled him to leave British India and seek international support for India’s independence. The escape remains one of the most dramatic episodes in modern Indian history. Timings Museum Timings Tuesday to Sunday 11:00 AM – 6:00 PM Closed Mondays Select national holidays Visitors are advised to verify timings before planning their visit, especially on public holidays. Entry Fee Indian Visitors: INR. 50 Foreign Visitors: INR. 50 Children up to 12 years: INR. 20 Donations are welcomed for the maintenance of the museum and research activities. Best Time to Visit The ideal months are: October November December January February The pleasant winter weather makes exploring Kolkata’s heritage attractions comfortable. Morning visits are recommended to avoid crowds and enjoy the museum at a relaxed pace. How to Reach Netaji Bhawan By Metro The nearest metro station is Netaji Bhavan Metro Station on Kolkata Metro’s North-South Line, just a short walk from the museum. By Taxi Taxis and app-based cabs are readily available throughout Kolkata. By Bus Several city buses connect Elgin Road with Esplanade, Park Street, Ballygunge, Gariahat, and Howrah. By Train Howrah Railway Station: approximately 8 km Sealdah Railway Station: approximately 6 km By Air Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport is approximately 22 km away. Nearby Attractions After visiting Netaji Bhawan, you can also explore: Victoria Memorial St. Paul’s Cathedral Birla Planetarium Maidan Rabindra Sadan Nandan These attractions can easily be combined into a full-day Kolkata heritage itinerary. Visitor Tips Allocate 1–2 hours for your visit. Photography policies may vary inside the museum; check before taking pictures. Read the exhibit descriptions to fully appreciate the historical context. Wear comfortable footwear, as the museum spans multiple floors. Visit during weekdays for a quieter experience. Combine your visit with nearby heritage attractions in central Kolkata. Interesting Facts About Netaji Bhawan Built in 1909 by the Bose family. Netaji escaped from this house on 16 January 1941. The original Wanderer car is preserved here. The museum is managed by the Netaji Research Bureau. Thousands of original documents relating to Netaji are preserved in its archives. It remains one of the most visited historical museums in Kolkata. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 1. Why is Netaji Bhawan famous? It is the ancestral home of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and the place from where he made his historic escape from British surveillance in 1941. 2. Where is Netaji Bhawan located? It is located on Lala Lajpat Rai Sarani (formerly Elgin Road) in central Kolkata. 3. Is there an entry fee? No. Entry to the museum is free for all visitors. 4. What are the museum timings? The museum is generally open from 11:00 AM to 4:30 PM, Tuesday through Sunday. 5. Can visitors see Netaji’s original car? Yes. The famous Wanderer car used during his escape is one of the museum’s main attractions. 6. How much time is required to visit? Most visitors spend 1–2 hours exploring the museum. 7. Is photography allowed? Photography policies may vary. Visitors should confirm with museum staff before taking photographs. 8. Which is the nearest metro station? Netaji Bhavan Metro Station is the closest metro station. 9. What is the Netaji Research Bureau? It is a research institution dedicated to preserving and studying the life, writings, and legacy of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose. 10. What are the nearby attractions? Popular nearby attractions include Victoria Memorial, St. Paul’s Cathedral, Birla Planetarium, Maidan, Rabindra Sadan, and Nandan. 11. Is Netaji Bhawan suitable for children? Yes. The museum provides an engaging educational experience for children, students, and families interested in Indian history. 12. What is the best time to visit Netaji Bhawan? The winter months from October to February are the most comfortable for sightseeing in Kolkata.
